Hi all,

Following up with two practical allocation approaches and the pros/cons from a rev-rec perspective. Attaching a worked example (Draft_Invoicing_Table_QtyRamp.xlsx) — short summary below.

Option A — Fiscal-year tranche invoices (what Ava asked):
- Invoice 1 (FY26): X% of prepay mapped to services delivered in FY26; Invoice 2 (FY27): Y%; Invoice 3 (FY28): remainder.
- Revenue recognition: Redwood books the full cash as deferred revenue on receipt and amortizes to revenue over the service period assigned to each tranche.
- Pros: matches your FP&A needs; avoids large variances in reported revenue for ChronoHealth.
- Cons: requires a clearly defined service period allocation in the SOW and acceptance of prorated recognition rules.

Option B — Usage-proportional amortization with single upfront invoice:
- Single invoice for the full prepay at signature; revenue recognized monthly based on agreed ramp schedule (e.g., 40/35/25 over three years).
- Pros: simpler invoicing, aligns revenue to actual consumption; Redwood’s AR team processes one invoice.
- Cons: ChronoHealth gets one payment in FY26 which may complicate your internal budgeting unless you accept a memo allocation for FP&A.

ASC 606 note: both are ASC 606-compliant; the key control is the identified performance obligation(s) and the allocation of transaction price over the performance periods. We recommend documenting the allocation table in the SOW and including acceptance criteria or usage milestones if you want usage-anchored amortization.

Action items:
- Ava: confirm which option ChronoHealth prefers or whether you want a hybrid (split invoices but amortize against actuals).
- Monica: see attached draft invoice table. I can convert this to journal-entry guidance for your controller once you confirm allocation.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

1) Can Redwood issue separate invoices that are payable at signature but labeled for each fiscal year (e.g., "Payment for FY27 services") so our AP can code them directly?
2) If usage lags significantly behind the assumed ramp, will Redwood allow a small true-up credit or adjustment mechanism? We are comfortable with the amortization approach but need a way to avoid paying for capacity we are not using in year 1.

Hi Ava — quick answers and an operational proposal.

1) Invoice labeling: yes. We can create three payable line items (FY26 / FY27 / FY28) on signature and mark each with a separate invoice number. Each will be payable on receipt but coded in the invoice metadata to the target fiscal year for your AP/ERP.

2) True-up mechanism: we can include a quarterly usage review clause with a capped true-up credit. Proposed guardrails:
- Quarterly review windows aligned to your fiscal quarters.
- If actual usage < 70% of planned ramp for a given year, ChronoHealth can request a true-up credit up to 20% of that year's tranche, to be applied against subsequent invoices or as a credit note.
- Any true-up requires sign-off from both finance teams.

I attached a draft invoicing table with invoice dates, amounts by fiscal tranche, and an example credit note line. If that works, we can bake the exact percentages into the SOW payment schedule.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
